ai.title: Stricter criteria for updating a knowledge file
ai.summary: The `generateKnowledgeFiles` function in `backend/src/generate-knowledge-files.ts` now enforces stricter criteria for updating knowledge files. The prompt logic was refined to require a very strong affirmative response to specific questions regarding missing context or undelivered outcomes before any file update is triggered. Examples of meaningful and meaningless changes were adjusted to better guide the LLM's decision-making process. This change aims to reduce noise in knowledge files by ensuring only highly relevant and non-derivable information is recorded.

eli5.text: The system that decides whether to save helpful notes about your coding conversations now has a higher bar for what gets recorded. When the assistant and you are working together, it used to be fairly quick to trigger a saved knowledge file if it thought your back-and-forth was meaningful. Now, it requires a very strong reason to save something, like you had to correct the assistant because it missed important context, or you expected something from it that it didn't deliver and couldn't easily figure out how to do better next time. Minor or obvious changes, like adding simple features, no longer get saved automatically, so your saved notes stay cleaner and more focused on genuinely useful insights.

ai.title: Refactor file requesting to consolidate prompts and remove index-based
ai.summary: Simplified `requestFilesPrompt` by removing the distinction between 'key' and 'non-obvious' file requests based on iteration indices. The `generateFileRequests` function now executes a single set of parallel requests (Key, Example, Non-Obvious, Test/Config) using a consistent `countPerRequest` of 5, eliminating the previous dynamic prompt generation that relied on `index * 2 - 1`. `checkNewFilesNecessary` now returns a `duration` metric, and `getRelevantFiles` hardcodes `claudeModels.haiku` instead of accepting a model parameter. This reduces complexity in the file selection heuristic while maintaining the same overall request structure.

eli5.text: The system that picks which code files matter to you now asks the AI helper just one consistent way, instead of switching between two different styles of requests. This means you get the same kind of file suggestions each time without any hidden variation, and the helper logs a little more detail about how long it took to decide. Nothing about what files get suggested changes, so your experience stays the same.

ai.summary: backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts replaces promptClaude with promptOpenAI for new-file necessity checks. Model shifts from claudeModels.haiku to models.gpt4omini. Message array restructures to include system prompt as first element.

eli5.text: The assistant now asks a different AI model (GPT-4o-mini) instead of Claude to decide whether it needs to read more files before answering you. If you look at the logs of this file-reading decision, you will notice it was faster, because GPT-4o-mini answers the 'YES' or 'NO' question more quickly than Claude's Haiku model did. This affects everyone who triggers the assistant to request additional files, since the decision now travels through the new model.

ai.title: Refine knowledge file generation prompt logic
ai.summary: Updated prompt instructions in `backend/src/generate-knowledge-files.ts` to prevent chain-of-thought leakage and enforce explicit no-op output. The model is now instructed to consider questions internally without writing them, and to output 'No knowledge file changes needed' if criteria are unmet, replacing the previous silent skip. This change aims to improve reliability in determining when to create or update knowledge files.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to figure out whether a new knowledge file should be saved, it now keeps its own working thoughts completely private instead of spilling them into its reply, and if the answer is no, it says exactly 'No knowledge file changes needed' rather than leaving a blank silence. This only affects the internal decision-making step that runs behind the scenes when you're saving notes from a conversation; you wouldn't see this unless you were inspecting those logs, and even then it just means the logs stay cleaner and easier to interpret.

ai.title: Halve PAID and PRO PLUS credit limits and add Stripe customer
ai.summary: The `CREDITS_USAGE_LIMITS` map in `common/src/constants.ts` now sets PAID to 5,000 and PRO_PLUS to 27,500 credits for production users (halved from 10,000 and 55,000), with matching reductions in the local overrides. A new script `scripts/migrate-stripe-customers.ts` migrates existing Stripe customers from the $99/month tier to a new price using `env.STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID` and `env.STRIPE_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID`, records prior usage via `billing.meterEvents.create` with `event_name: 'credits'`, and applies coupon `wwu4ER94` with `proration_behavior: 'none'`. These changes align with the commit message 'Cut costs and credits by half' and update billing documentation in `backend/src/billing/billing.knowledge.md` and `web/knowledge.md` with migration best practices. The pricing page in `web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx` also adjusts displayed prices, now showing Pro at $49/month, Pro Plus at $249/month, and Team at $99/seat/month.
ai.evidence: The diff in `common/src/constants.ts` edits `CREDITS_USAGE_LIMITS` for both local and production branches, halving PAID from 10,000 to 5,000 and PRO_PLUS from 55,000 to 27,500 (production) and from 10,000,000 to 5,000,000 and PRO_PLUS from 55,000,000 to 27,500,000 (local). It also adds a new script `scripts/migrate-stripe-customers.ts` that reads `env.STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID` and `env.STRIPE_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID`, updates Stripe subscriptions for customers on the $99/mo plan, records usage via `billing.meterEvents.create` with `event_name: 'credits'`, and applies a coupon `wwu4ER94` with `proration_behavior: 'none'`.
ai.migration: Existing subscribers on the $99/month tier must be migrated using the new script `scripts/migrate-stripe-customers.ts`, which reads STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID and STRIPE_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID; users on higher tiers will see their credit allowances halved, and operators should verify coupon and price IDs before running.
ai.unknowns: The actual rollout status of the new Stripe price IDs and whether the coupon applies to all customers or only a subset.

changes.what: Halved PAID and PRO_PLUS credit limits in CREDITS_USAGE_LIMITS for both local and production environments.
Added migrate-stripe-customers.ts to migrate Stripe subscriptions to new price IDs, record usage via meter events, and apply a coupon.
Added documentation on subscription migration best practices including usage preservation and pagination.
Updated displayed pricing tiers for Pro, Pro Plus, and Team plans.
Expanded documentation on Stripe integration including subscription updates and item handling.

ai.title: Fix subscriptionactive check on cancellation
ai.summary: In `web/src/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts`, `subscription_active` now checks `!!newSubscriptionId` instead of `usageTier === 'PAID'`. This ensures the flag reflects actual subscription presence rather than tier status, preventing incorrect active states during cancellation or downgrade events. Scope limited to Stripe webhook handling.

eli5.text: When your subscription is being changed, whether you're canceling it or switching to a different plan, the system now looks at whether you actually still have an active subscription ID to decide if your account should show as active. Previously, it was only checking if your plan tier was set to a paid level, which could wrongly show you as still having an active subscription even while the cancellation or downgrade process was already underway. This prevents confusion where the system might think you still have full access when you're in the middle of losing it.

ai.title: safeReplace escapes $ in file-block string replace
ai.summary: Added safeReplace in common/src/util/string.ts to escape $ in replacement strings. Replaced String.prototype.replace in backend/src/process-file-block.ts with safeReplace. Prevents $1, $&, and other special patterns from being interpreted as capture group references during file block processing. Internal refactor in core and shared utilities.

eli5.text: When the assistant rewrites a section of a file using a search-and-replace operation, any dollar signs ($) in the replacement text no longer get misread as special formatting commands by the system. The assistant can now safely include literal dollar signs in the content it writes back, so file edits that previously produced garbled output now stay intact. This affects anyone whose file edits contain dollar signs, and you would notice that replaced blocks keep their original punctuation instead of showing broken characters.

ai.title: Remove git mv/rm preference in system prompt
ai.summary: System prompt guidance for file operations now recommends standard `mv`/`rm` commands instead of `git mv`/`git rm`. This change in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` removes the requirement that file moves and deletions be tracked by Git for refactoring requests.

eli5.text: The assistant will now use basic file-moving and file-deeting commands instead of those tied to version control tracking, which means file organization tasks happen the same way whether or not they're logged as code changes. This affects anyone the assistant helps move or delete files during code work. If you watched the assistant in action, you'd notice it using simpler commands for these operations instead of ones that update the project history automatically.

ai.title: Consolidate drizzle-orm to 0.38.0 in common
ai.summary: Removed `drizzle-orm` and `drizzle-kit` from `backend` and `web` package manifests, consolidating dependencies into `common`. `common/package.json` updated to `drizzle-orm@0.38.0` and `drizzle-kit@0.28.1`, moving `drizzle-kit` from peerDependencies to dependencies. This centralizes ORM version management across the monorepo.

eli5.text: The app now pulls in its database helper tools from one shared location instead of maintaining separate copies in different parts of the system. If you were looking behind the scenes, you'd notice that the backend and web portions no longer carry their own copies of these tools, while the shared core now handles both the current version and its setup helper. This is live today and primarily affects developers working on the app's internal structure.
